SPHERES: What the world receives as the work
The challenge the life keeps setting
What the body broadcasts when it is well
The ground the radiance stands on
How the mind values and selects
The prosperity that falls out of the rest

Signature.what: What the world receives when you are doing the thing you are for.
Signature.how: Start here because it is the only sphere other people can see directly. Read the gate, then ask whether the work you actually do resembles it. Most of the path's usefulness comes from that one comparison.

Crucible.what: The ground the work stands on — and the challenge the life keeps setting until it is met.
Crucible.how: Always the exact opposite of the first. Read them as a pair: the work is what you give, the crucible is the condition under which giving it is possible. When the work stalls, the fault is usually here.

Aura.what: What the body broadcasts when it is well, before you have said anything.
Aura.how: Design side, so you cannot see it and other people can. Ask someone who knows you what they notice when you walk in. Their answer will be closer to this gate than your own guess.

Objective.what: The ground the aura stands on. The body's own direction, underneath the mind's.
Objective.how: Opposite the third, as the second was opposite the first. This is the quietest sphere on the path and the one that does not argue — it simply stops cooperating when it is ignored.

Gravity.what: What arrives without being sought. The magnetism, not the effort.
Gravity.how: Read this before any sphere about wanting. It describes what comes toward you when you are not reaching, which is the only reliable evidence of what the design actually does.

Logos.what: How the mind values and selects — what it counts as worth thinking about.
Logos.how: Not intelligence. Taste. This gate says what your mind finds interesting enough to keep, which decides everything you will ever be good at.

Pathos.what: How feeling is spent. The currency and the temper of it.
Pathos.how: Read alongside the sixth. The pair describes what you value and how you spend — a mismatch here is the ordinary source of feeling both principled and broke.

Sophos.what: The deeper valuation, running unconsciously beneath the stated one.
Sophos.how: Design side, so expect it to present as distortion until it is named. Read the engine first, then ask what you keep choosing that you have never justified.

Ethos.what: The vocation's engine. What the life is actually powered by.
Ethos.how: Deepest sphere on the path and the last one that is about you alone. Everything after this turns outward.

Spirit.what: What is transmitted outward — what people take from you and carry on.
Spirit.how: You do not choose this and cannot much steer it. Read it as a description of your effect, not your intent.

the Diamond Self.what: The prosperity that falls out of the rest. Not a reward — a by-product.
the Diamond Self.how: Read last, always, and read it as conditional. The Diamond Self is what accumulates when the other ten are worked; taken on its own it is a horoscope, which is the one thing this system is not.

KARAKA_GLOSS.Atmakaraka: The soul's own significator — the single most important body in the chart. Follow it through every division; whatever it does everywhere is what the life is for.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Amatyakaraka: The minister. How the soul's purpose gets administered and by what means.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Bhratrikaraka: Siblings, courage, the guru. What stands beside.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Matrikaraka: The mother, and the capacity to be nourished.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Putrakaraka: Children, students, and what is generated and passed on.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Gnatikaraka: Kin, obstacles, and the daily friction that shapes.
KARAKA_GLOSS.Darakaraka: The partner — not who is wanted, who arrives.

KARAKA_METHOD: Rank the seven visible planets by degree within their sign, highest first. The highest is the Atmakaraka; the descending ranks fill the cabinet.

1.h: 13°15′–18°52′ Scorpio · Anuradha (lines 1–3) → Jyeshtha (lines 4–6), seam in line 4 · Algiz→Sowilo · Mars
1.e: Creative self-expression run through two engines in sequence. In the Anuradha lines, the work is a devotion: what descends is the summons to make — the vision arriving from beyond the maker; what ascends is the maker's discipline, the daily return to the desk as offering. The result (honor) accrues only when both travel: vision received and discipline supplied. In the Jyeshtha lines, the finished work enters the field of rank: what descends is the attack — the claim the work makes on attention; what ascends is the defense — the maker's protection of its singularity. The seam at line 4 is where private devotion becomes public contest, and it is the most sensitive degree of the gate: work crossing from altar to arena.
1.l: You make as an act of worship in the lower lines — the practice kept whether or not the summons feels present, trusting descent to meet discipline. In the upper lines you let the work attack: put it forward first, take the summit of expression without apology.
1.d: You withhold the unripe work — descension as craft, the deliberate delay that honors the summons by refusing to hand it a fetus. In the upper lines you defend: end collaborations that would dilute, decline the arena until the work can hold it.
1.r: Freeze is the common presentation: the work never releases, perfectionism narrated as standards — the pole above (the summons) has gone unfelt, and the person is all ascending discipline toward a vision they no longer receive. Medicine is the light gift: restore the receiving before touching the output problem. Flood appears as recognition-hunger — work attacking constantly, defended nowhere, the devotion pole abandoned; medicine is the dark gift, the withheld release.
1.a: When you sit down to make — does anything arrive, or are you alone at the desk? (Seam line 4: ask both this and who is the work fighting?)

2.e: The keeper of direction run through the growth engine. What descends is the plant-pattern — direction arriving as a form the life wants to take, not a decision. What ascends is the water — the resources, attention, and nourishment the keeper controls. Creation results when water is given to the pattern and only the pattern. Gate 2 does not generate direction; it recognizes the seed already proposing itself and steers by irrigation.
2.l: You grow the way — direction exercised as cultivation, making the true path so lush that others (and your own will) follow it without being argued onto it. The magnetism of this gate is literally fertile ground.
2.d: The withheld watering. You let a wrong direction die of thirst — no confrontation, no debate, just the quiet redirection of every resource away from it until it composts. In practice this is the most efficient course-correction on the wheel and the least visible.
2.r: Flood: everything green gets watered — projects, people, possibilities — and the garden chokes; the ascending pole (selective water) is being spent without the descending pattern being consulted. Medicine is the dark gift: institute the drought. Freeze: direction awaited from others while your own seed-pattern desiccates — the descent unreceived. Medicine is the light gift: ask what form the life is already proposing, then water only that.
2.a: If you stopped watering everything for a month — what would still be alive, and is that the garden you meant?

3.h: 26°22′ Aries–02°00′ Taurus · Bharani (opening of line 1) → Krittika (rest), seam at 26°40′ Aries · Uruz→Thurisaz · Mars
3.e: Ordering the newborn chaos, run almost entirely through the burning engine with Bharani's fingerprint on the threshold. The gate opens — its very first arc — inside Yama's mansion: every beginning this gate governs starts with a removal, something carried out of the birth-room before order is possible. Then Krittika takes over: what descends is heat — the transformative pressure of the new; what ascends is light — the discernment that shows which mutations are viable. Purification of the beginning results when the new thing is both pressured and seen.
3.l: You midwife the new order in the open — apply the heat of constraint to the newborn project while keeping the light on, so everyone (including you) can watch what survives and why. Innovation as visible trial.
3.d: You cull. The mutation that will not live is cut early, deliberately, before it consumes the litter's milk — and per the Bharani sliver, its removal is escorted: named, ended, and carried out, not left to die in a drawer.
3.r: Flood: serial scorched beginnings — heat applied to every sprout, nothing rooting; the light pole (discernment) is missing, and the culling happens by burnout instead of by hand. Medicine is the dark gift consciously taken: choose one cut, perform it, escort it out. Freeze: nothing new is attempted because beginnings hurt — the heat pole refused. Medicine is the light gift: one small beginning run as an open, witnessed trial.
3.a: Of the last three things you started — did you end any of them on purpose, or did they all just die?

4.h: 18°52′–24°30′ Leo · Purva Phalguni entire · Nauthiz · Sun
4.e: The answer-generating mind run through the procreation engine — and the localization is exact: Gate 4 does not know, it conceives. What descends is the question, the beloved — the open problem in its full attraction. What ascends is the answering impulse, the lover. The fetus their meeting conceives is the formula: an answer that is genuinely new but genuinely unborn — it must gestate before it is a fact. This gate's entire pathology and entire genius come from confusing conception with birth.
4.l: You court questions — hypothesis as fertile play, the delight of the almost-right answer enjoyed as pleasure rather than defended as truth. Your formulas are offered as conceptions: "here is what the question and I made last night; let's see if it lives."
4.d: You refuse to answer. The formula is withheld — deliberately unconceived — until the question has ripened into one worth impregnating. Doubt is kept open on purpose; the mind practices contraception.
4.r: Flood is the signature: answers spawning compulsively, conceived by anxiety on any question that wanders past, each one announced as a birth. The ground pole (the actual, present lover — your own considered impulse) is absent; the answers are fathered by fear. Medicine is the dark gift: a formal fast from answering. Freeze is rarer: no answer ever hazarded because none is certain — the descent (the question's attraction) unfelt. Medicine is the light gift: restore play before rigor.
4.a: That answer you just gave — did you conceive it in pleasure or in panic?

5.h: 11°22′–17°00′ Sagittarius · Mula (lines 1–2) → Purva Ashadha (lines 3–6), seam in line 3 · Tiwaz→Berkano · Jupiter
5.e: Fixed rhythm run through two engines split at the root. In the Mula lines, rhythm meets the root-wrench: what descends is the breaking-apart of dead pattern; what ascends is the crushing of its residue. These lines govern the destruction of false rhythm — the routines that have become cages. In the Purva Ashadha lines, rhythm meets the early waters: strength descends, connection ascends, and the kept pattern produces luster — the ritual timing that visibly invigorates a life. The gate's full teaching: sacred rhythm requires periodic root-demolition; a rite never broken is eventually a tomb.
5.l: You keep the pattern that strengthens — the daily rite held with enough connection (to season, to body, to purpose) that it waters the root rather than merely repeating. Waiting as active attunement to natural timing.
5.d: You break a rhythm at the root. Deliberately, completely — the habit razed, the schedule salted — because it had begun to keep you rather than the reverse. The lower lines authorize demolition the upper lines then rebuild upon.
5.r: Freeze presents as paralysis dressed as patience: waiting that has lost its descending pole (the strength the rite was channeling) and become mere postponement. Medicine is the light gift — reconnect the rhythm to what it feeds. Flood presents as rhythm-shatter: routines breaking themselves and reforming as compulsions, the root-wrench turning unaimed. Medicine is the dark gift performed once, consciously, at a chosen root — which typically stops the unconscious breakage.
5.a: Your most fixed routine — does it water you, or are you its keeper now? (Seam line 3: ask both this and what rhythm needs razing?)

6.h: 22°38′–28°15′ Virgo · Hasta (line 1 sliver) → Chitra (rest), seam at 23°20′ · Jera · Mercury
6.e: The membrane of intimacy run through the jewel engine, with the hand at the threshold. The gate opens in Hasta: first contact is literally manual — what may pass the membrane is decided by touch, the skilled admitting hand. Then Chitra governs the body of the gate: what descends is the law — the pattern intimacy ought to take, the terms; what ascends is the truth — what the two bodies and histories actually are. Friction is the lapidary process: conflict here is the cutting of the relational jewel, truth faceted against law until the bond is both real and beautiful.
6.l: You open by hand and cut in the open — admit the right other deliberately, then treat every conflict as facet-work: the flaw named so the ornament can be true. Peace, in this gate, is a product of well-run friction, never its avoidance.
6.d: You close the hand. Entry refused without apology; the membrane sealed while the law of the matter is weighed. And when a bond has become paste — beautiful terms over a dead truth — you break the ornament deliberately.
6.r: Flood: the membrane opens and closes on ambient weather — conflict discharging wherever emotional pressure is highest, intimacy leaking into whoever stands closest. The ground pole (truth: what is actually so between these particular people) has been abandoned for reactivity. Medicine is the dark gift: seal first, weigh second. Freeze: the membrane armors shut, all law and no admitted truth, conflict avoided until it detonates. Medicine is the light gift: one small friction run openly as facet-work.
6.a: Your last real conflict — was it cutting the stone, or just heat escaping?

7.h: 13°15′–18°52′ Leo · Magha (line 1) → Purva Phalguni (lines 2–6), seam at 13°20′ · Hagalaz→Nauthiz · Sun
7.e: The role of leadership run through the throne of the dead and the marriage bed in sequence — and the sequence is the teaching. Line 1 sits in Magha: all authority in this gate is inherited, and the inheritance is only legitimate if the predecessor was mourned — the leader must first bury whoever held the role before, including their own prior self. Lines 2–6 sit in Purva Phalguni: legitimate leadership then operates procreatively — what descends is the led (the beloved), what ascends is the leader (the lover), and direction is not imposed but begotten in the people, conceived so they carry it as their own.
7.l: You lead as delegate and begetter — the seat occupied with its dead honored, direction seeded in others so that the army moves because it has conceived the plan, not because it was ordered.
7.d: You abdicate on purpose. The role left cleanly, the mourning done in advance, the crown passed while it still has value — the ruler who knows the throne's occupant must sometimes be carried out for succession to be real. You can also refuse to beget: withholding direction from a people who must conceive their own.
7.r: Freeze: influence exercised from behind the throne while responsibility is disclaimed — the Magha pole unmet, the predecessor (often a father, a founder, an old self) unburied and still ruling through you. Medicine is the light gift, which here begins with a funeral. Flood: direction begotten on everyone — every room impregnated with your plans, none carried to term. Medicine is the dark gift: abdicate somewhere, formally.
7.a: Who held your role before you — in the org, in the family, in yourself — and is you buried?

8.h: 24°30′ Taurus–00°08′ Gemini · Mrigashira entire · Ansuz→Raidho · Venus
8.e: Contribution run through the deer's-head engine. What descends is extension — the outward search for where the authentic thing belongs; what ascends is weaving — the integration of the found place, the thread actually worked into the collective cloth. The gate's promise (fulfillment; the world made enjoyable) is delivered only by the shuttle's full cycle: out to find the audience, back to weave the contribution in. Gate 8 fails in both directions available to a shuttle.
8.l: You extend and weave — carry the authentic contribution outward with real searching (not broadcast: search, with the deer's attention), and when the true loom is found, commit the thread and stay for the weaving.
8.d: You withhold the thread. Refusal to be woven into fabrics that would waste you — the contribution kept back from the almost-right audience, the collaboration declined, the platform left. In a creator's practice this is the discipline that protects a voice from dilution-by-opportunity.
8.r: Flood: the search that cannot stop extending — contribution chasing audience after audience, exposure mistaken for weaving, a life of publishing into the wind. The ground pole (weaving: staying, integrating, belonging to one cloth) is missing. Medicine is the dark gift: withdraw from all looms but one, and weave there. Freeze: the thread hoarded — nothing offered because no loom is worthy. Medicine is the light gift: extend once, small, real.
8.a: Where are you actually woven in — not followed, not seen: woven?

9.t: The Taming Power of the Small
9.e: Focus run wholly through the root-wrench — the only concentration gate on the wheel powered by a demolition engine, which explains everything about it. What descends is breaking-apart: the overwhelming whole fractured into workable grains. What ascends is crushing: the residue of each grain fully processed, reduced, finished. The result — destruction that destroys destruction — localizes as focus that demolishes overwhelm itself: the small tames the great by taking it apart at the root.
9.l: You dismantle the mountain into stones and address one stone. Detail-power aimed: the root of the problem found and worked, the seventeen-headed task decomposed until each head is mortal.
9.d: You raz the distraction field. Deliberately — tabs closed, projects killed, inputs severed — not as productivity hygiene but as conscious demolition: the destroyer aimed at what destroys your attention.
9.r: Flood: everything is taken apart and nothing reassembled — analysis as rubble-making, detail crushing the purpose it serves; the wrench turns on whatever is nearest, including the work itself. Medicine is the dark gift aimed: give the demolition one legitimate target (the actual distraction-source) and the indiscriminate wrecking typically stops. Freeze: focus refused because the whole is too large to enter — the breaking-apart pole (which is the gate's own gift) unreceived. Medicine is the light gift: fracture the task once, visibly, into three grains, and touch one.
9.a: What are you grinding right now — the problem's root, or just whatever's in reach?

10.h: 28°15′ Sagittarius–03°52′ Capricorn · Uttara Ashadha entire · Berkano→Ehwaz · Jupiter
10.e: The behavior of the self run through the unassailable-ground engine. What descends is winnable strength — the capacity for authentic conduct that this particular self actually possesses; what ascends is the winnable goal — a way of being in the world that this self can genuinely sustain. Unchallengeable victory localizes as conduct that cannot be argued with because nothing false props it up: the self lived so accurately that attack finds no purchase. Self-love, in this gate, is not a feeling; it is a fortification produced by right-sized authenticity.
10.l: You behave as yourself at exactly your own scale — no performed virtue, no borrowed conduct — and the position becomes untakeable. All the gods endorse it because it is defended by nothing but its truth.
10.d: You decline the contest. Every invitation to defend what needs no defense is refused; critics arrive at the arena and you are not there. Concession of the argument, retention of the ground.
10.r: Freeze: conduct becomes performance for invisible judges — the goal pole has been swapped for an unwinnable one (universal approval), so behavior is endlessly adjusted and never at rest. Medicine is the light gift: name one way of being you can actually, fully sustain, and hold only that. Flood: victory claimed in rooms where no contest occurred — self-assertion spraying at allies; the strength pole discharging without an aim. Medicine is the dark gift: withdraw from all uncontested arenas.
10.a: What part of how you act could you defend forever — and what part are you defending right now instead?

11.h: 22°38′–28°15′ Sagittarius · Purva Ashadha (lines 1–4) → Uttara Ashadha (lines 5–6), seam in line 5 · Berkano · Jupiter
11.e: The gate of ideas run through the two Ashadhas in sequence — early waters, then unassailable ground; the declaration, then the victory. In lines 1–4, ideas operate as invigoration: what descends is their strength, what ascends is their connection to hearers, and the result is luster — ideas that visibly refresh a whole valley whether or not they are ever implemented. This gate does not build; it waters. In lines 5–6, past the seam, an idea occasionally crosses into Uttara Ashadha and becomes structural: the image whose victory is inherent, needing no argument.
11.l: You pour the images out as irrigation — teaching, philosophy, imagery offered to strengthen the thinking of others, with no claim staked on implementation. And you recogniz the rare line-5/6 idea that has crossed into inevitability, and let that one stand undefended.
11.d: You declare the unwinnable war of ideas on purpose — the provocation designed to strengthen the opponent's own thought; or withhold the finishing idea so the audience can win with it themselves. The teacher's contraception: the answer kept back for the student's conception.
11.r: Flood is the signature: ideas flooding without banks — every notion announced at conception, the harvest of images rotting unstored, the person mistaking their irrigation function for a construction contract they then fail. The ground pole (connection: actual hearers, actual fields) is missing; the water pours on rock. Medicine is the dark gift: a withholding practice — ideas kept until asked for. Freeze: the images dammed entirely for fear none is defensible; medicine is the light gift — pour without defending.
11.a: Who is actually watered by your ideas — names, not audience?

12.e: The voice run through the return engine — and the localization dissolves this gate's apparent paradox (a Gemini articulation gate whose name is Standstill). What descends is the weather: the receptive moment, the rain that comes when it comes. What ascends is growth: the matured feeling the voice has been ripening in silence. Speech in this gate is recovery — the word that restores scattered substance — and it only works in season. Standstill is not the gate's failure; it is the gate's method: the voice withdraws so that speech can return with interest.
12.l: You speak when the rain comes — articulation timed to genuine receptivity, and the words carry disproportionate restoring power precisely because they were grown, not manufactured. The socially shy voice that, in the right moment, says the thing that rebuilds someone.
12.d: You go silent on purpose. Withdrawal wielded — the absence of your voice made palpable as communication; the word banked until it can come home changed.
12.r: Freeze: standstill becomes mute exile — the silence no longer ripening anything, the descent pole (the returning season) no longer trusted or watched for, so the voice simply dies in storage. Medicine is the light gift: watch for one rain and speak once into it. Flood: unseasonal confession — the caution collapsing periodically into a torrent that scatters what it meant to restore. Medicine is the dark gift made conscious: silence chosen and named stops being silence that bursts.
12.a: What are you currently ripening in silence — and are you watching for its weather, or just hiding?

13.e: The listener run through the hundred-physicians engine. What descends is pervasion — other people's stories, secrets, and wounds soaking into your from the whole field; this gate cannot not-receive. What ascends is the support — the vessel: the practice, boundary, circle, or confidant that holds you while the material works through. The result (the world freed of calamity) localizes precisely: confession heard by a held listener is treated; the same confession poured into an unheld listener is merely relocated.
13.l: You witness as suture — the listening that itself heals, offered from inside a maintained vessel. The keeper of the collective story who has a keeper of your own.
13.d: You seal the archive. What you have heard is kept — deliberately, permanently — from those who would misuse it; and you refuse new confessions when the vessel is full. The closed circle as treatment.
13.r: Flood is nearly universal in this gate: pervasion without a vessel — every wound in the room migrating into the listener, the archive festering, cynicism accreting as untreated material calcifies ("everyone's story is the same story"). The support pole is missing. Medicine is the dark gift: seal first — a formal intake-stop — then build the vessel before reopening. Freeze: the archive locked even to yourself, listening withdrawn entirely; medicine is the light gift received — you confess to a held listener before you resume being one.
13.a: You hold everyone's secrets. Name what holds you.

14.h: 24°30′ Scorpio–00°08′ Sagittarius · Jyeshtha (lines 1–5) → Mula (line 6), gandanta seam at 0°00′ Sagittarius · Sowilo→Tiwaz · Mars
14.e: Wealth-power run through the eldest's engine, with the wheel's water-fire abyss opening at its crown. In lines 1–5, resources are Jyeshtha's business: what descends is the attack — the conquest of fortune, skills converted to holdings; what ascends is the defense — stewardship, the protection of what is won for those it serves. The hero-result localizes as the wealthy elder: possession legitimated by protection. Then line 6 crosses the gandanta into Mula, and the engine inverts: breaking-apart descends, crushing ascends, and the gate's final teaching is that great possession must periodically pass through the root-wrench — wealth uprooted from meaning must be returned to the root or it becomes the destroyer.
14.l: You conquer and steward — fortune aggressively won and then aimed, spent on the clan's behalf, defended as a granary rather than displayed as a trophy. At line 6: you consciously returns wealth to the root — endowment, sacrifice, the fortune deliberately planted back.
14.d: The potlatch. You ruin your own holdings on purpose — burn the granary that has become the master, uproot the fortune that owns you — the sovereign act of a holder who refuses to be held.
14.r: This is the wheel's deepest money-knot and it runs both types at once: flood as fortunes conquering their holder (accumulation compulsive, defense abandoned — medicine is the dark gift, one deliberate divestment), and freeze at line 6 as the gandanta signature — wealth-destruction cycles that feel fated, gain and ruin alternating without a hand on either. There the medicine is naming the seam itself: the client with line 6 activations is shown that the uprooting is in the architecture — and can therefore be performed consciously (endowment, tithe, sabbatical) before it performs itself.
14.a: Does your wealth serve anything that would survive it? And — line 6 — when it burns down, who lit it?

15.h: 28°15′ Gemini–03°52′ Cancer · Punarvasu (lines 1–5) → Pushya (line 6), seam at 3°20′ Cancer · Kenaz→Gebo · Mercury
15.e: The love of humanity run through the return engine, ripening at its final line into the udder. In lines 1–5, the gate's famous embrace of extremes is Punarvasu's recovery function: what descends is the weather — humanity's wild variety of tempos arriving like seasons; what ascends is growth — the flow wide enough to receive each extreme back into the herbs-and-trees of the common life. Gate 15 is where the scattered rhythms of the species come home. At line 6, past the seam into Pushya, the welcome becomes rite: hospitality as worship, the guest received as the god, the flow itself made a devotional act.
15.l: You restore the extremes — the too-fast and the too-slow welcomed back into the current without being normalized; your own wide swings held as range rather than failure. At line 6, you host as liturgy.
15.d: You keep the strange rhythm on purpose — refuse the average for yourself or another, protect the outlier tempo against every pressure to regularize. The deliberate defense of extremity as a form of love.
15.r: Flood: the flow swallows you — every arriving tempo overwrites your own, the welcome so total there is no host left; the growth pole (your own root-rhythm) unsupplied. Medicine is the dark gift: keep one strange rhythm of your own inviolate. Freeze: the extremes rejected, in others and in yourself — the weather pole refused, life regularized into a drought. Medicine is the light gift: readmit one extreme, yours first.
15.a: When everyone's rhythms flow through you — what tempo is yours?

16.h: 05°45′–11°22′ Gemini · Mrigashira (line 1) → Ardra (lines 2–6), seam at 6°40′ · Raidho · Mercury
16.e: Skill run through the search and the storm in sequence. Line 1 sits in Mrigashira: every skill begins as a finding — the art glimpsed like the deer, the identification of what is worth mastering; this line is the taste that precedes talent. Lines 2–6 sit in Ardra: what descends is the hunt — repetition, the ten-thousand-fold chase of the form; what ascends is the reaching — the moments of genuine arrival where the skill consolidates. Achievement results only from the full storm-cycle: chase and catch, practice and consolidation. Enthusiasm is this engine's fuel gauge, not its product.
16.l: You practice as pursuit — repetition kept vivid by the hunter's attention, each session a chase with a real quarry; and you marks the catches, letting arrival register in the body so the skill banks.
16.d: You stay in the storm on purpose — refuse the premature stage, withhold performance until the skill is real; the deliberate obscurity of the woodshed years.
16.r: Flood: enthusiasm performs before it can execute — the identification (line 1's taste) mistaken for the possession, versatility as a carousel of week-old passions. The reaching pole is missing: nothing is ever consolidated. Medicine is the dark gift: one skill, sealed practice, no audience, a season. Freeze: perpetual preparation — the hunt never permitted to end in a catch, performance deferred forever. Medicine is the light gift: schedule one small arrival and let it count.
16.a: Name a skill you've actually landed — not loved, not started: landed. What did the landing feel like?

17.e: Opinion run through the swift-arrival engine — and the localization corrects this gate's usual reading. Gate 17's speed is not glibness; it is triage. What descends is the confusion to be treated — the disordered situation arriving as patient; what ascends is the organizing view — opinion as remedy, structure applied to chaos. The result (freedom from disease) localizes as: the group's thinking cured of its tangle. But the engine's law is medical: a remedy is dosed to a diagnosed patient. Opinion delivered to no diagnosed need is not treatment; it is medication scattered in the street.
17.l: You arrive first with the organizing view and administers it as medicine — check that the confusion wants treating, dose the opinion to the actual tangle, and stop when structure takes.
17.d: You withhold the diagnosis. First on the scene, sees the whole disorder, says nothing — the speed converted to private reconnaissance, the opinion banked until treatment is requested or required.
17.r: Flood: opinions bolt riderless — every passing confusion prescribed for, the view arriving before the person it was for, speed mistaken for depth. The patient pole is missing: no one asked. Medicine is the dark gift: prescribe only on request for a season. Freeze: the view suppressed entirely because past doses were spat out; medicine is the light gift, re-dosed — one opinion, one asking patient, full delivery.
17.a: Your last strong opinion — who was the patient, and had they come to you?

18.t: Work on What Has Been Spoilt
18.h: 03°52′–09°30′ Libra · Chitra (lines 1–3) → Swati (lines 4–6), seam in line 3 at 6°40′ · Eihwaz · Venus
18.e: Correction run through the jewel and then the wind — two different repairs, split at the seam. In the Chitra lines, the spoilt thing is worked lapidary-fashion: law descends (the pattern the thing ought to have), truth ascends (what it actually is), and correction cuts toward the jewel — critique as craftsmanship, the flaw named so the form can be perfected. In the Swati lines, the deeper cases: what is spoilt past cutting is given to the wind — dispersal descends, transformation ascends, and the correction is release: the pattern scattered entirely so the material can take new form. Knowing which repair a spoilt thing needs — the file or the wind — is this gate's mastery.
18.l: You repair toward the jewel where a jewel is possible: the inherited pattern corrected with a craftsman's love for the corrected thing. And where it is not, you scatter cleanly — the spoilt pattern released without a salvage obsession.
18.d: You dismantle the heirloom. The fathers' work judged against truth rather than piety; the ancestral pattern deliberately broken up and given to the wind — the correction tradition itself cannot perform on itself.
18.r: Flood: criticism blows through every room uninvited — fault-finding running on old parental voltage, everything condemned, nothing repaired; the law pole has decayed into mere reflex and no jewel is ever intended. Medicine is the dark gift aimed ancestrally: find the inherited critical pattern and dismantle that, and the ambient criticism drains. Freeze: flaws seen and never spoken, the correction swallowed until it sours into contempt; medicine is the light gift — one flaw named aloud with the finished jewel described.
18.a: When you criticize — whose voice is it, and what would the repaired thing actually look like?

19.e: Sensitivity to need run through the hundred-physicians engine. What descends is pervasion — the wants and hungers of the field soaking in: this gate feels every unmet need in the room as pressure on its own skin. What ascends is the support — provision, the concrete answer to need, but dosed from a held vessel. The result (the world freed of calamity) localizes as: need met before it becomes crisis. The engine's law, as everywhere in Varuna's mansion, is that the physician must be held to heal — approach from an unheld healer transmits the disease of neediness even as it feeds.
19.l: You approach with support — attunement converted to provision: the resource, the touch, the acknowledgment delivered where the need actually is, from a self that has its own supply lines.
19.d: You seal the membrane. Triage: the one need refused so ten can be met; the deliberate non-answer to a want that would consume the answerer. Not coldness — dosage.
19.r: Flood is the signature: every need in the field floods you, approach becomes appeasement, the boundary dissolves and the physician sickens patient by patient — the support pole (your own vessel) unfunded. Medicine is the dark gift: a formal triage list, some needs named refused. Freeze: the sensitivity armored over entirely, needs sensed and coldly unanswered until the pressure detonates as resentment; medicine is the light gift — one need, met fully, from a vessel checked first.
19.a: Of everything you sense people needing from you — what do you need, and who's on that?

20.e: Presence run through the deer's-head engine. What descends is extension — awareness reaching into the now, the sighting: the deer glimpsed in this instant's clearing. What ascends is weaving — the sighted moment integrated, allowed to change the fabric of the one who saw it. Fulfillment localizes as presence that lands: the now not merely observed but metabolized. The gate's voice ("I am, now") is the engine's exhaust — real when a sighting has been woven, noise when it hasn't.
20.l: You speak the now you see — the immediate word that names what is actually here, with the deer's quality of attention: alert, undemanding, whole-bodied. Your observations land because they were sighted, not composed.
20.d: You watch without announcing. Silent presence as tracking — the moment observed and left undisturbed, the sighting kept, awareness wielded as pure receptivity with the mouth closed.
20.r: Flood: the now chatters itself away — awareness narrated instead of inhabited, a running commentary that reports constantly and weaves nothing; existence performed as feed. The weaving pole is missing. Medicine is the dark gift: a silence practice — sightings kept unspoken until one actually changes you. Freeze: presence withdrawn into pure spectatorship, life watched from the treeline and never entered; medicine is the light gift — one sighting spoken into the room where it happened.
20.a: Of everything you noticed today — did any of it change you, or was it all just feed?

21.h: 09°30′–15°08′ Aries · Ashwini (lines 1–4) → Bharani (lines 5–6), seam in line 5 at 13°20′ · Fehu→Uruz · Mars
21.e: Control run through the physicians and then the death-lord — surgery, in exactly that order. In lines 1–4, management is Ashwini's business: the wound descends (the mismanaged resource, the failing operation), the remedy ascends (swift decisive intervention), and the result is the household cured — control as the surgeon's legitimate authority over the operating field. In lines 5–6, past the seam into Bharani, control matures into its final competence: knowing what must be removed — ended, fired, sold, carried out — and escorting it. The whole gate: first the scalpel, then the stretcher.
21.l: You take charge fast to heal — money, territory, operations gripped decisively and briefly, the intervention scaled to the wound, authority relinquished as the patient stabilizes. At the seam and above: the ending performed with escort, the removed thing honored out of the house.
21.d: You remove what you govern. The deliberate amputation — the role eliminated, the product killed, the tie cut — chosen while it is still elective surgery rather than emergency.
21.r: Flood is the classic presentation: control gripping everything within reach — other people's kitchens micromanaged, authority metastasizing past its operating field; and what should be removed is instead managed forever, because removal ends the control. The Bharani pole is missing. Medicine is the dark gift: one genuine removal, escorted, this month. Freeze: control abdicated entirely after past overreach — the household visibly hemorrhaging while you refuse the scalpel; medicine is the light gift — one bounded intervention with a named end-date.
21.a: What are you still managing that you already know needs removing?

22.e: Social openness run through the shepherdess's engine. What descends is the source — your emotional richness, the milk; what ascends is the need — the actual calves: the specific others whom this openness is for. Nourishment-of-the-world localizes as grace that feeds: charm, listening, beauty of manner deployed so that people leave your presence fuller. The engine's law is Pushan's: milk in the cow feeds no one, and the shepherd counts heads — grace that doesn't reach a particular calf, and grace whose giver goes unfed, both fail the engine.
22.l: You grace the room by feeding it — openness aimed at the actual hungers present, the social artistry that leaves each person specifically nourished; and you are fed in turn, because you permit it.
22.d: You withdraw the milk. Deliberate coldness where warmth would be squandered — grace refused to those who bite the feeding hand, the wean performed on those who should graze on their own.
22.r: Flood: the mood nurses everyone and starves itself — charm switched on for strangers, off for kin, the giver depleted and unfed; the calf-pole has become "everyone," which is no one. Medicine is the dark gift: a named short list of who actually gets the milk. Freeze: openness curdled after going unmet — the grace withheld from all, sourness worn as discernment; medicine is the light gift — one person fed deliberately, and one feeding received.
22.a: Who exactly are you feeding — and when did someone last feed you?

23.h: 18°52′–24°30′ Taurus · Rohini (lines 1–4) → Mrigashira (lines 5–6), seam in line 5 at 23°20′ · Ansuz · Venus
23.e: The stripping word run through growth and then the search. In the Rohini lines, translation is horticulture: what descends is the strange insight — the pattern from Gate 43's inner ear arriving as seed; what ascends is the water of ordinary language. The essential word is the seed planted plainly enough to grow in other minds — this gate's genius is not simplification but germination. In lines 5–6, past the seam into Mrigashira, the word's function shifts: the essential utterance that sends hearers searching — the koan-function, the sentence that extends the listener beyond what it says.
23.l: You translate the strange into the fertile — insight stripped to what can root in a hearer's actual soil, then watered with patience while it grows. At the top lines: the deliberate koan, the word that opens a hunt.
23.d: The assassin's sentence. One stroke, deliberately aimed, that fells a bloated consensus — the assumption split apart in a single utterance. Used rarely, on structures that deserve it.
23.r: Flood: the stripping tongue runs unbidden — simplification amputating rather than clarifying, rooms split that the speaker needed whole, the assassin's stroke landing on friends. The soil pole is missing: no one's ground was consulted before planting. Medicine is the dark gift formalized — the cutting sentence reserved, written before spoken, aimed only at structures. Freeze: the insight withheld because past plantings were trampled; medicine is the light gift — one seed, one chosen soil, plain water.
23.a: Before you say the stripped-down thing — whose soil is it landing in, and can it grow there?

24.h: 07°38′–13°15′ Taurus · Krittika (lines 1–2) → Rohini (lines 3–6), seam in line 3 at 10°00′ · Thurisaz · Venus
24.e: The returning mind run through fire and then growth — and the sequence is the cure for this gate's famous rumination. In the Krittika lines, the thought that circles back meets the burn: heat descends (the pressure of the unresolved), light ascends (discernment of what in it is viable), and the mull's first function is incineration — most of what returns should be burned on arrival. In the Rohini lines, what survives the fire is planted: pattern descends, water ascends, and the returning thought finally roots — rationalization ripening into genuine realization. The engine's law: no planting without prior burning; a mind that skips the fire plants its weeds.
24.l: You return with fire first — the recurring thought met each time with discernment (is this viable or residue?), and the viable remainder given real water: time, articulation, growth into conclusion.
24.d: You burn the loop. The obsessive circuit deliberately incinerated — the dead question's mental ground salted, the 3 a.m. return refused fuel — because it has been through the fire enough times to be certified residue.
24.r: Freeze is the signature: the mind returns and returns and returns — the same thought reheated nightly, never burned, never planted, the groove worn into a trench. Both poles are missing, but the fire first: medicine is the dark gift — a formal verdict practice (each recurring thought gets one written judgment: burn or plant) which restores the Krittika lines' function. Flood is rarer: every returning thought planted uncritically, the mind a garden of rooted grievances; medicine is the same verdict practice weighted toward the burn.
24.a: The thought that keeps coming back — burn or plant? You're allowed exactly one answer.

25.h: 28°15′ Pisces–03°52′ Aries · Revati (lower arc) → Ashwini (upper arc), the triple ring-closure at 0°00′ Aries · Othala→Fehu · Jupiter
25.e: The spirit of the self run across the wheel's only true seam — the point where three ring-closures coincide: last mansion into first, last rune into first, wheel-end into wheel-start. The Revati arc runs the shepherdess's engine at world-scale: what descends is everything the closing world still holds; what ascends is everything in it that must be fed before the crossing. The Ashwini arc runs the physicians' engine at dawn-scale: the new world's first wounds descending, the first remedies ascending. Between them, at the zero point, is the gate's actual nature: the love that survives the crossing because it carries nothing — universal love as the toll-free passage. Othala's estate closes; Fehu's herd walks out of the gate.
25.l: You love without ledger on both shores — provisioning what ends with the shepherdess's completeness, arriving in what begins with the physician's speed, and holding the crossing itself as identity: not the estate, not the herd, but the one who walks between.
25.d: You let the old world end. The deliberate non-rescue of what belongs to the closing age — the inheritance declined, the estate unshouldered — innocence wielded as the refusal to carry the dead world into the living one.
25.r: The gandanta signature runs deeper here than anywhere: the self dissolves at every threshold — love bleeding out unbanked (flood: the calf-pole gone universal, medicine the dark gift, a ledger kept for one season as scaffolding), or each new beginning arriving skinless, wounded by a crossing it cannot remember (freeze: the descent — what the new world actually offers — unreceived; medicine the light gift, the physician's arc entered consciously: name three things the new shore has already given). In any Dharma Design this gate is read first, as the chart's world-crossing; with a design-side activation, expect the client to have no language for it until the seam is named — and expect the naming to move them.
25.a: What are you still carrying from a world that has ended — and what has the new one already handed you that you haven't picked up?

26.t: The Taming Power of the Great
26.h: 17°00′–22°38′ Sagittarius · Purva Ashadha entire · Berkano · Jupiter
26.e: The claim run through the early-waters engine. What descends is strength — the genuine value of the thing being declared: the product, the vision, the self; what ascends is connection — the actual relationship to the hearers whose attempt the claim will invigorate. Luster results when both travel: the declaration that strengthens the tribe to act, shining because it is both strong and connected. This gate's salesmanship is the invigoration function wearing a market costume — the early oath spoken so a people dares.
26.l: You sell the truth with early water — the pitch that bridges from what exists to what could, delivered to hearers you are actually in relation with, its exaggerations disciplined by the connection: you will face these people at harvest.
26.d: You tame the great by trickery — the conscious feint, the strategic overclaim deployed with full knowledge of the gap and a plan to close it; the trickster's declaration that creates the very strength it announces.
26.r: Flood: the pitch pitches itself — memory editing in the seller's favor unbidden, the declared victory replacing the attempted one, luster borrowed against harvests never brought in. The connection pole has dropped: the hearers have become "market," faceless, so nothing disciplines the claim. Medicine is the dark gift made honest — the feint performed knowingly (with the gap written down privately) rather than believed. Freeze: nothing claimed because claims feel like lies — the strength pole undervalued; medicine is the light gift: one declaration made to named hearers, sized to what you can face them with.
26.a: Your current pitch — could you deliver it looking at the faces of people you'll see at harvest?

27.e: Care run through the blade-flame — the gate of nourishment powered by the burning engine, which is the whole teaching. What descends is heat: care as transformation — the raw made sustaining, the dependent made capable, the protected made strong; feeding, in this gate, always cooks. What ascends is light: the visibility of the care — who is fed, why, at what cost, seen by all including the carer. Purification results when care both transforms and is witnessed: the guardian flame in the open hearth.
27.l: You cook for the tribe — care that changes its recipients: the meal that strengthens, the protection that trains, the support engineered toward its own obsolescence. And the hearth is lit where everyone can see it, your own plate included in the count.
27.d: You burn the spoiled portion. The dependency cauterized — the care withdrawn from a tie that has begun to rot both parties, the cut sealed in one clean act. Krittika's blade is what keeps this gate's love from becoming a swamp.
27.r: Flood is the signature: caring scorches — overfeeding, overprotecting, the flame cooking what it was warming, capability burned out of the cared-for; and your own plate stays empty because the light pole is off: no one, least of all you, is watching the actual accounting of the care. Medicine is the dark gift: one dependency named and cauterized. Freeze: care withheld entirely after past scorchings — the hearth cold, hunger all around; medicine is the light gift — one act of care performed in full visibility, your plate filled first.
27.a: Who has your care made stronger — and who has it made softer? Be exact.

28.h: 02°00′–07°38′ Scorpio · Vishakha (line 1) → Anuradha (lines 2–6), seam in line 2 at 3°20′ · Algiz · Mars
28.e: The struggle for meaning run through the forked gateway and then the bridge of devotion. Line 1 sits in Vishakha: the fight begins as agriculture — plowing descends, harvest ascends, and the question of any struggle is the field's: what fruit justifies this furrow? Lines 2–6 sit in Anuradha, and the engine deepens: ascension descends... rather, something in the struggler rises, something beyond the struggle descends to meet it, and the fight becomes an offering — struggle consecrated, the game worth playing because the playing is devotion. The gate's famous question (is life worth its weight?) is answered differently by each engine: Vishakha says by the harvest; Anuradha says by the worship.
28.l: You plow toward named fruit in line 1 — risk taken because the harvest is real and reckoned. In the body of the gate, you consecrate the fight: the struggle chosen as offering, difficulty embraced because something rises in you when you meet it and something answers.
28.d: You end the meaningless fight. Walks off the field where nothing worth harvesting grows and nothing descends to meet the effort — the concession that keeps the life, the game abandoned as an act of devotion to what deserves the struggle instead.
28.r: Flood: struggle seeking itself — risk taken for voltage, purposeless fights generated to hide the fear of a purposeless life inside; both engines running empty (no named fruit, nothing descending). Medicine is the dark gift: a formal audit — every current fight tagged harvest, offering, or neither, and the neithers abandoned. Freeze: all struggle refused, life flattened into safety, the weight-question answered by never lifting; medicine is the light gift — one difficulty deliberately taken up as offering.
28.a: Your hardest current fight — what's the fruit, or what descends to meet you in it? If the answer is neither, why are you still on the field?

29.h: 24°30′ Leo–00°08′ Virgo · Purva Phalguni (lines 1–2) → Uttara Phalguni (lines 3–6), seam in line 3 at 26°40′ · Nauthiz→Isa · Sun
29.e: The yes run through courtship and then covenant — the two Phalgunis in their canonical order. In lines 1–2, saying yes is Purva Phalguni's conception: desire meets desire, and the commitment is conceived in pleasure — the whole-body yes that this gate's power depends on. In lines 3–6, past the seam into Aryaman's mansion, the yes is signed: what each party brings is put on the table, and the union prospers only by honest mutual contribution. The gate's teaching in engine form: a commitment conceived without pleasure carries the grimness as a birthmark; a commitment signed without terms bankrupts a house. The abyss is crossed by both — the joyful conception and the honest contract.
29.l: You commit whole-body and on terms — the yes said from actual desire (lines 1–2 consulted first), then formalized with both dowries visible: what you bring, what it will cost, what the other house supplies.
29.d: The whole no. The yes withheld from the union whose prosperity would cost the self — the refusal delivered before the abyss, complete, unhedged, contraception of the commitment.
29.r: Flood is the signature: yes escaping before the question finishes — commitment bled across everyone who asks, conceived by neither pleasure nor terms, the person perpetually mid-abyss on vows they cannot recall making. Medicine is the dark gift: a moratorium — every request answered no by default for a season, yeses requiring a written case. Freeze: no yes ever whole — commitments entered at half-body, exits pre-planned; the pleasure pole unfelt. Medicine is the light gift: one small commitment chosen for desire alone and said completely.
29.a: Your biggest current yes — was it conceived in pleasure, and did both houses put their contribution on the table?

30.h: 24°30′ Aquarius–00°08′ Pisces · Purva Bhadrapada entire · Ingwaz→Dagaz · Saturn
30.e: Desire run through the two-faced fire. What descends is the good of all beings — the world-serving face of the wanting: what this hunger, fed, would give everyone. What ascends is the good of the gods — the vertical face: what the hunger serves that is higher than appetite, the altar it burns on. The result (the support of the whole world) localizes as desire that holds worlds up: feeling as sacred fuel. This gate's fever is the strongest emotional fire on the wheel, and the engine's demand is absolute — it must serve both faces or it serves neither, and a fire serving neither takes the house.
30.l: You feed the fever to the altar — the wanting consciously fueled, aimed, and offered: desire yoked to what it would give the world and what it burns for above, the fantasy become vocation.
30.d: You starve a hunger on purpose. The ascetic's deliberate fast — clinging renounced not from fear of feeling but as fire-management: this want unfed so the flame purifies instead of spreads.
30.r: Flood: the fever dreams you — wanting attaching to whatever passes, each new object burning bright and abandoned charred, the fire jumping the altar; both faces unserved, the heat serving only its own continuation. Medicine is the dark gift: one named fast, held for a season, which teaches the fire it has a keeper. Freeze: desire suppressed wholesale as dangerous — the person fireproofed and cold, the world unsupported by what they were built to burn for. Medicine is the light gift: one hunger chosen, both faces named (whom it serves below, what it serves above), and fed.
30.a: Your strongest current wanting — name one being it would concretely serve, and one altar it burns on. If you can't name either, it has you.

31.e: The leading voice run through the throne of the dead. What descends is the mourning — the honored weight of every voice that held this influence before: the tradition, the office, the ancestors of the role. What ascends is the leaving — the predecessor's genuine departure, which alone makes the seat available. Union-with-the-ancestors localizes politically: legitimate influence is transmitted, not seized — the voice that leads carries the dead's authority precisely because the dead have been both honored and released. Gate 31 speaking without this engine is a microphone with no signal: heard, followed briefly, hollow.
31.l: You speak as the delegate of the seat — influence exercised in conscious continuity with those who held it before, the "we" of your leadership a real lineage rather than a rhetorical crowd.
31.d: You vacate. The resignation performed while the office still has honor — influence surrendered so the seat survives the sitter; the deliberate hand-over that makes you ancestor rather than obstacle.
31.r: Freeze is the signature: the seat speaks and the man mouths it — every sentence pre-polled, leadership performed for the portrait gallery, the predecessor (a founder, a father, a former self) unmourned and still issuing orders through you. The leaving pole is missing. Medicine is the light gift, begun as a funeral: name whose voice the influence actually channels, honor it formally, and release it. Flood: influence seized without transmission — authority claimed over people whose dead you have not honored; medicine is the dark gift in miniature — vacate one claimed seat.
31.a: When you speak as a leader — whose voice is underneath yours, and have you buried them or are they using you?

32.e: Continuity-instinct run through the forked gateway. What descends is the plowing — the investment of seasons: effort, capital, loyalty committed to a field before any fruit exists. What ascends is the harvest — the actual yield by which every continuity is finally judged. The fruit-result localizes as duration that bears: the instinct this gate carries is precisely the farmer's judgment — which fields justify their plowing, which traditions still fruit, which ventures will still be yielding in ten years. Fear of failure is this engine's exhaust-smell: the plowing pole felt as risk.
32.l: You back the bearing crop — continuity-sense wielded as venture wisdom: the tradition preserved because it still fruits, the investment held through fallow seasons because the yield-judgment was sound, the lot-cup shaken with a steady hand.
32.d: You let a harvest fail on purpose. The field deliberately released — the tradition retired, the venture sunset — because its fruit has turned or its plowing now costs more than its yield; the other fork taken against sentiment.
32.r: Freeze is the signature: fear of failure preserving everything and risking nothing — all fields kept as fallow insurance, duration become taxidermy, the instinct for what would bear never tested because testing risks the loss it exists to sense. The plowing pole is refused. Medicine is the light gift: one field chosen by the instinct and actually plowed — committed to, in public, with seasons allowed. Flood: serial preservation-abandonment cycles, everything backed then dropped; medicine is the dark gift formalized — deliberate sunset of the weakest holding, which teaches the instinct that endings are survivable and steadies the rest.
32.a: What are you preserving out of fear that you'd never plant today — and what would you plant if failure were survivable?

33.e: Withdrawal run through the throne of the dead — and where Gate 31 uses Magha's engine to speak, Gate 33 uses it to archive. What descends is the mourning: the era honored as it closes, the experience grieved into meaning. What ascends is the leaving: the actual exit — from the field, the cycle, the relationship — that alone converts experience into transmissible memory. Union-with-the-ancestors localizes as the living archive: the elder who left the field carrying the story is how the dead speak to the unborn. Retreat, in this gate, is a priestly office; privacy is the vault where experience is embalmed into teaching.
33.l: You retreat to hold the memory — the withdrawal performed as archive-work: the era mourned, the lessons extracted, the story kept until the moment of transmission, then told as inheritance.
33.d: You leave without farewell. The clean exit — the mourning completed in advance, the door closed on an era with a steady hand and no forwarding address; departure wielded as the final word.
33.r: Freeze is the signature: retreat happening to you mid-sentence — the withdrawal reflex firing unchosen; secrets hoarding themselves; the archive locking until even you lose the key, experience accumulating unmourned and therefore untransmissible. The mourning pole is missing: you leave but never grieves, so nothing converts. Medicine is the light gift: one closed era formally mourned (written, spoken, ritualized) and one story from it deliberately transmitted. Flood is rarer: every experience narrated instantly, nothing vaulted, the archive open-plan; medicine is the dark gift — a withholding period between living and telling.
33.a: Of the eras you've left — which did you actually mourn, and who has heard what you learned there?

34.e: Pure power run wholly through the root-wrench — the wheel's strongest motor mounted on its demolition engine. What descends is breaking-apart: force arriving as the capacity to take structures down. What ascends is crushing: the thoroughness that finishes what the breaking began. The result — destruction that destroys destruction — is this gate's entire ethics in one clause: Gate 34's power is display-worthy only by the wreckage it chooses; aimed at what destroys, it is the land-clearing that makes every building possible; aimed at nothing, it is busyness as bulldozer.
34.l: You clear land — strength applied to what must come down so what must rise can: the obstruction razed, the dead structure removed, the field left genuinely buildable. Power made beautiful by its target-list.
34.d: You uproot your own dependency. The masterless act: your strength's reliance on whatever it has been serving — an employer, a role, an audience, an addiction — deliberately broken at the root, the motor reclaimed.
34.r: Flood is the signature: power discharging wherever it stands — busyness razing fields nobody wanted cleared, strength serving whoever grabs the handle, the motor running all night in an empty lot. The aim (a named destroyer as target) is missing. Medicine is the dark gift: identify what currently owns the strength and uproot that service first; an aimed engine stops idling. Freeze: power suppressed as dangerous after past collateral — the strongest person in the room acting weakest, the land uncleared; medicine is the light gift — one legitimate demolition chosen, performed, and completed to the crushing.
34.a: Your strength is running — who's holding the handle, and what would you aim it at if you were?

35.e: The hunger for experience run through the storm engine. What descends is the hunting — appetite for the next taste, the chase that makes this the wheel's most traveled gate. What ascends is the reaching — the arrival actually felt: the experience consummated, digested, converted to the wisdom this gate is supposed to accumulate. Achievement localizes as the rained-on field: progress is only progress if the storm that darkened the sky actually waters something. Gate 35's tragedy-pattern — "been there, done that, felt nothing" — is this engine running on its descending pole alone.
35.l: You progress through the storm — change pursued with the chase's full vividness and wrung for its rain: each experience closed, tasted to the bottom, banked as flavor before the next is opened.
35.d: You abandon the finished thing. Deliberately — the mastered game left mid-victory, the completed chapter closed without ceremony — because staying past the rain is just wetness; the storm-rider's discipline of moving when the field is watered, not when the crowd expects.
35.r: Flood is the signature: experience collected undigested — the reaching resetting before the grasping closes, boredom hunting you through your own achievements, a passport full of stamps and no weather. The consummation pole is missing. Medicine is the dark gift inverted into a completion practice: one past experience deliberately returned to and finished — written, told, ritually closed — which teaches the engine that arrival exists. Freeze: hunger suppressed after too many empty chases — novelty refused, the sky permanently clear and the fields dry; medicine is the light gift — one small new experience entered with a pre-committed digestion step.
35.a: Name the last experience that actually changed your flavor — not your resume. How long ago was that?

36.e: Crisis run through the shepherdess's engine — the darkening of the light powered by the mansion of nourishment, which reframes everything. What descends is the source: the emotional provisions this gate accumulates — every survived turbulence stored as milk. What ascends is the need: the next crosser — the person entering the dark water this gate has already crossed. Nourishment-of-the-world localizes as the wound become waybread: Gate 36's crises are provisioning runs; the depth of feeling gathered in the dark exists to feed those still in it. Inexperience is this gate's hunger for stores it doesn't yet have.
36.l: You carry others through the darkening — turbulence survived, rendered, and fed forward: the counselor, the initiator, the one whose presence in another's crisis says "this water is crossable; I have bread."
36.d: You enter the crisis deliberately. The initiatory dark chosen — the depth sought on purpose, with provisions packed and a return planned — because certain milk can only be gathered there.
36.r: Flood is the signature: crisis generated to feel the crossing — inexperience hurling itself at deep water unprovisioned, the drama nursing on whoever is nearest because the stores are empty and the hunger is real. The source pole (rendered, banked experience) is missing; the person is trying to feed others from crises they haven't digested. Medicine is the dark gift disciplined: no new voluntary dark until one past crossing is fully rendered — written, understood, converted to actual bread. Freeze: all depth avoided after a bad crossing — the emotional life kept in the shallows, the stores unrenewed; medicine is the light gift at minimum dose — accompany someone else's small crisis with what stores exist.
36.a: Your worst crossing — is it rendered into bread yet, or are you still just wet?

37.h: 05°45′–11°22′ Pisces · Uttara Bhadrapada entire · Dagaz · Jupiter
37.e: The hearth-bond run through the deep serpent's rain. What descends is the raining cloud: warmth, resources, and presence delivered as reliable climate — the steady affection a household can plant by. What ascends is the growing plant: each member's actual flourishing under that weather, which is the only honest measure of the bargain. Stability-of-worlds localizes as the kept covenant: Gate 37's famous "bargain" of belonging is meteorological — I rain, you grow, and the arrangement is renegotiated in the open when either fails. The serpent coiled beneath the floor is the depth this gate's warmth draws on: fed by fair terms, it stabilizes the house; ignored, it stirs.
37.l: You rain on the household — affection distributed as dependable weather rather than mood; the bargain kept and spoken: what each gives, what each grows, reviewed like a covenant rather than assumed like furniture.
37.d: You withhold the rain. The deliberate drought — warmth suspended, visibly and namedly, to renegotiate a one-sided bargain; the serpent's stillness as the message that terms have failed.
37.r: Flood: the weather of the house runs you — belonging purchased with endless small payments, affection leaking as appeasement, the covenant never spoken because speaking might end it; the growth pole unmeasured (no one asks whether anyone is actually flourishing). Medicine is the dark gift: one term named aloud and one payment suspended until it is met. Freeze: the rain stopped in unnamed resentment — the house drying out while everyone calls the tension mysterious, the serpent stirring beneath conversations about nothing; medicine is the light gift — the covenant spoken plainly, rain resumed on stated terms.
37.a: In your household's bargain — what do you give, what do you grow, and when did anyone last say it out loud?

38.h: 09°30′–15°08′ Capricorn · Uttara Ashadha (line 1) → Shravana (lines 2–6), seam at 10°00′ · Ehwaz→Mannaz · Saturn
38.e: The fight-for-what-matters run through unassailable ground and then the listening ear — and the sequence rewrites this gate's reputation. Line 1 sits in Uttara Ashadha: the stand taken on winnable ground — the stubbornness that cannot be moved because nothing false props it up.
